world.topic:
Locate the critical temperature T_c of the two-dimensional Ising model (square lattice, periodic boundaries, J = 1, no field) from simulations made with the given program `/initial-state/inputs/0/ising.py` (numpy only; `python3 ising.py --help`), and compare it with the exact value 2/ln(1+sqrt(2)) = 2.2692.

The study has three stages; each is designed from the result of the one before:

1. Pilot: L = 64, T from 1.5 to 3.5 in steps of 0.1, seeds 1 and 2, 20,000 measured sweeps after 2,000 burn-in. Locate the peak of the susceptibility.
2. Crossing: L = 32, 64 and 128 at 9 equally spaced temperatures from 0.12 below to 0.12 above the pilot's peak, seeds 1 to 3, 20,000 sweeps, keeping the time series (`--series`). Estimate T_c where the Binder cumulants of the three sizes cross, with a bootstrap 95% interval over seeds, and the integrated autocorrelation time of |m| at each point, to say whether 20,000 sweeps are enough.
3. Check: L = 256 at 5 equally spaced temperatures from 0.03 below to 0.03 above the stage-2 estimate, seeds 1 and 2, 10,000 sweeps. Say whether the L = 256 Binder values agree with the stage-2 crossing.

Deliver the data and analysis code of every stage, two figures (the pilot's susceptibility and heat capacity against T; the Binder cumulants of all sizes near the crossing), and a one-page report `report/report.md` (Markdown is enough) with T_c, its interval, the comparison with the exact value and what stage 3 showed. On this machine a single stage takes several minutes or more.
